summary: This resolution sets House floor procedures, including one hour of debate and a motion to recommit, for considering five joint resolutions that would disapprove National Park Service, Fish and Wildlife Service, and EPA rules on motor vehicles in Glen Canyon, longfin smelt protections, and California vehicle emission standards.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a procedural resolution to expedite consideration of joint resolutions disapproving certain agency rules. It contains no provisions related to appropriations, budgets, or federal expenditures.
No provisions in the bill address tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
The bill does not engage with healthcare policy, insurance, or medical regulations.
No connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill contains nothing related to immigration, borders, or visas.
No provisions touch on reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not address military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.

The resolution provides for expedited House consideration of five joint resolutions of disapproval targeting specific agency rules: National Park Service restrictions on motor vehicles in Glen Canyon, Fish and Wildlife Service endangered-species listing for the longfin smelt, and three EPA waivers allowing California to enforce stricter vehicle-emission standards (Advanced Clean Trucks, Advanced Clean Cars II, and Omnibus Low NOX). By facilitating congressional nullification of these environmental and emissions rules, the bill directly advances the limitation or rollback of environmental regulations.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, SNAP, Medicaid, or other safety-net entitlements.
The bill has no bearing on schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reform.
No provisions concern tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The bill contains no fiscal measures that would affect deficits or debt.
No content related to LGBTQ protections or related civil-rights issues.
The bill does not address foreign assistance or international aid.
No provisions touch on voting access, election administration, or voter ID.
The bill has no relation to technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions address labor law, union rights, or workplace regulations.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
